CHIEF COMPLAINT
Status post mitral valve repair follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 63-year-old female presenting for follow-up evaluation following mitral valve repair performed on 8/3/2020. She reports overall improvement since surgery and feels she is "pretty good" now. She continues to experience occasional chest pain and shallow breathing with exertion, which lasts only a few minutes and resolves with activity reduction. Symptoms recur approximately a couple times per month, with symptom-free periods lasting a couple of weeks between episodes. Patient reports good functional status and is learning to modify her activity level accordingly. She is compliant with medications using a reminder app. Initially experienced irritability with atenolol, but this side effect has resolved. Denies other new symptoms.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies new symptoms. Patient reports occasional exertional chest discomfort and dyspnea with exertion, both resolving with activity modification. No other systemic complaints elicited.

Mitral regurgitation
Atrial fibrillation
Diabetes mellitus

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Head and Neck: No jugular venous distention detected.
Lungs: Reduced breath sounds, clear to auscultation and percussion bilaterally.
Heart: Irregularly irregular rhythm consistent with atrial fibrillation. S1 slightly accentuated, no S3 gallop appreciated.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender.
Extremities: Trace peripheral edema noted bilaterally. No tenderness.

RESULTS
ECG from 12/26/2020: Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response. T-wave inversion anteriorly. No significant changes compared to previous study.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
63-year-old female status post mitral valve repair in 2020 presenting for routine cardiac follow-up. Patient is recovering nicely from surgery with good functional status. Atrial fibrillation is well controlled on current medical regimen. Continue current medications: Coumadin 4 mg daily, Lasix 4 mg daily, and Atenolol 50 mg daily. Encourage continued physical activity as tolerated. Patient counseled that activity modification with exertional symptoms is appropriate. Follow-up appointment in 6-9 months.
